before: (2) To address changes in passenger-demand and road-traffic statistics that reduce the relevance of historical experience, this thesis develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR) based on Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR). Recent rewards and disagreement among action-value estimates are used to adjust conservatism during training. Training stabilization is combined with a learnable baseline action and a neural correction, while soft symbolic constraints guide holding actions and their responses to changes in the state. Bus policies are evaluated with their trained parameters fixed. With generalized passenger time cost as the training objective, CS-BAPR reduces mean per-passenger generalized time cost by 0.083% to 0.549% relative to RE-SAC across six scenarios covering routine demand, single and repeated demand surges, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand. Mean planned-headway deviation and forward-backward headway imbalance decrease by 7.35 to 12.09 seconds and 11.88 to 20.08 seconds, respectively. These results show average improvements over RE-SAC in passenger service and headway control under the tested demand changes.
